Ava Chen: proposing a new 'stability index' metric to sit alongside our existing card health heuristics. Combine ECC/Xid rates, thermal excursions, and transient network packet drops into a single decaying score per card per region.
Rakesh Patel: sounds helpful — how do you plan to weight transient vs persistent signals?
Ava Chen: goal is to penalize persistent regressions more. sketch: 70% persistent signals (repeat XID/ECC over 24h), 20% thermal events (over 1h spikes), 10% transient network packet loss bursts. decay window 7 days but with fast half-life for thermal spikes.
Marta Lopez: +1. We need actionable thresholds for runbooks. If stability_index < 0.4, auto-mark node for investigation; if <0.2, schedule drain + replacement.
Jon Becker: what about reserved capacity impacts? some regions have high dedicated pools; we should adjust SLOs to be weighted by committed capacity so tenants on reserved capacity don't get hit by noisy neighbors during drain.
Li Wei: agree. we can compute a region-weighted SLO: availability = 1 - (error_tokens_weighted_by_commit / total_committed_tokens). that way enterprise reserved usage influences the alert priority.
Ava Chen: draft PromQL for the stability index panel (very rough):
```promql
# per GPU card: weighted sum of normalized signals
(sum by(card) (
  rate(gpu_xid_errors_total[1h]) * 0.5 +
  increase(gpu_ecc_uncorrectable[24h]) * 0.3 +
  max_over_time(gpu_temp_high{job="nvml"}[1h]) * 0.2
) ) / (1 + sum by(card) (rate(gpu_xid_errors_total[7d])))
```
Rakesh Patel: nice. can you add a query for correlated multi-card blips in a rack? that helped us catch the switch flake last month.
Ava Chen: yep — using vector join on node and rack labels, then a heatmap of cross-card XID correlation:
```promql
sum by(rack) (increase(gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])) / sum by(rack) (increase(gpu_requests_total[5m]))
```
Marta Lopez: for alerts, suggest two tiers: P1 for cross-card correlation > 0.05 in production racks, triggers immediate mitigation (evacuate, notify SRE), P2 for single-card stability_index drop triggers ops workqueue.
infra-bot: scheduled job gpu-health-aggregator ran at 2026-01-10T04:00Z, snapshot written to s3://redwood-telemetry/gpu/snapshots/1767654321.json :white_check_mark:
Jon Becker: cost question — more aggressive drains increase re-provision churn. can we simulate monthly replacement rate and estimate incremental reserved hours?
Li Wei: we can. I'll add a Monte Carlo sim using current decay + replacement policy to the Optimize team dashboard. should give $ delta per policy.
Ava Chen: UX for Grafana: single overview row per region with small multiples for top 5 worst racks, then a cross-region summary showing weighted SLO and change vs baseline. add a sparklines column for stability_index trend.
Rakesh Patel: can we gate the roll-out behind a canary? let's only enable auto-drain in 1 region and send alerts elsewhere for 2 weeks.
Marta Lopez: agreed. I'll update the runbook with exact steps: 1) annotate node, 2) cordon, 3) drain with `rctl drain --grace=300 --node=$NODE`, 4) replace card and run nvml burn test, 5) uncordon.
Jon Becker: please include cost owner as approver for auto-replace, especially for Dedicated customers.
Ava Chen: action items: (Ava) push grafana dashboard PR with panels+promql, (Rakesh) implement alerting rules + canary toggle, (Li) run cost sim and post numbers, (Marta) update runbook and ops playbook.
Rakesh Patel: I can take alert rules. tagging @Jon and @Marta for approvals when ready. :thumbsup:
Marta Lopez: will review runbook and add escalation matrix.
Li Wei: starting cost sim now.
Ava Chen: thanks all — let's reconvene after canary run. :rocket:
